setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt. The branch's own shell singleton is edited in place; teardown discards it with the branch.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "shell-editor-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for shell-editor skill evals"

evals.name: submenu-with-two-wired-views
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: add a 'Tools' group to the app's left navigation with two entries — one opening a hub and one opening a grid. Use components that already exist on this branch or in one of its referenced packages (at least one from a referenced package), and make sure both open with every parameter they expect.
evals.expected_output: The own shell row's menubar gains one submenu item (hasSubmenu true) whose menubar holds two view items with viewType hub and grid; each viewConfig.moduleId is the target component's own package (a referenced package where applicable), configParameters carries an entry for every target inParam with string values; validate runs before the write.
expectations: The own shell row is located by applicationId == branch id and isExternal == false (or via 'get shell shell' / 'source branch shell' with the returned id checked); no dependency package's row is edited and no shell is created
menubar gains one item with hasSubmenu true, a snake_case id, and a label, containing exactly two child items
Both child items are view items (viewType + viewConfig), not flow items, and neither child is itself a submenu
One child has viewType "hub" and the other viewType "grid", each matching the actual type of the referenced component
Each child's viewConfig.moduleId equals the package that owns the referenced component, and at least one is a referenced package rather than the shell's own package
For each target, viewConfig.configParameters has one entry per target inParam (optional ones included), and every entry's value is a string
All item ids are snake_case and unique among their siblings
The shell description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate shell' run before 'dxs configuration upsert shell' (or before the documented fallback write)

evals.name: toolbar-flow-item
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: add a toolbar button with a help icon that, when clicked, writes 'help requested' to the browser console and shows an info toaster. Also tell me whether I could put the same button in the left navigation instead.
evals.expected_output: A flow item {id, icon, label, flowConfig{flowId}} is added to toolbar, a matching embedded cti-9 flow is added to flows[] with that referenceName, and the response explains that flow items are toolbar-only (in menubar validate fails 'Menu item should have a view type defined').
expectations: toolbar gains an item with a snake_case id, an icon, and flowConfig.flowId set (no viewType/viewConfig on that item)
flows[] contains an embedded flow with configurationTypeId 9 whose referenceName equals the toolbar item's flowConfig.flowId
Existing flows[] entries, menubar items, and onInitFlowConfig are preserved unchanged
The response states that a flow item is not allowed in menubar (navigation entries must be view items) and cites or paraphrases the 'Menu item should have a view type defined' validation error
The response notes that validate does not catch a flowId that does not match any flows[] entry, and the agent checks the match itself
The shell description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate shell' run before 'dxs configuration upsert shell' (or before the documented fallback write)

evals.name: harden-on-init
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: make the app set the browser title to '<app name> <environment name>' when it loads, and log the signed-in user's username through a backend function for usage tracking. Users must never be locked out of the app if any of this fails.
evals.expected_output: onInitFlowConfig binds an on_init embedded flow in which every step (title assignment via $workspace.title from $context.app.name / $context.env.name, the backend logging call) is wrapped in its own try/catch; the username is derived inside a backend function via GetCurrentUserInfo rather than from a UI-tier global; validate runs before the write.
expectations: onInitFlowConfig.flowId names an embedded flow present in flows[]
The title is set through $workspace.title (the shell's own IShell surface), not through $shell
Every independent step in on_init is inside its own try/catch block (no top-level statement that can throw uncaught)
The username is obtained server-side in a backend function (e.g. $apis.<Pkg>.FootprintApi.GetCurrentUserInfo) — on_init does not read a user-identity global
The response states that on_init runs on every app mount including Preview builds, so an uncaught error could break app load
Existing on_init code (if any) is preserved, not replaced
The shell description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate shell' run before 'dxs configuration upsert shell' (or before the documented fallback write)
